top_news.title: Unsupervised Latent Space Alignment with Hyperspherical Geodesic Matching
top_news.dek: Researchers propose a method for aligning neural network latent spaces without requiring shared sample correspondences.
top_news.brief: The paper introduces Hyperspherical Geodesic Matching to align independently trained latent spaces. By leveraging the geometric properties of latent representations, the approach avoids the need for anchor-based supervision, addressing a common bottleneck in unsupervised model alignment.
top_news.image_alt: Abstract diagram showing two latent spaces being aligned via hyperspherical mapping

top_news.title: Manage agents, tools and skills at scale with AWS Agent Registry
top_news.dek: AWS has launched a centralized, governed registry for managing AI agents, tools, and skills at scale.
top_news.brief: AWS Agent Registry provides a searchable catalog to help organizations track ownership, review status, and discovery of internal AI resources. It aims to solve fragmentation issues as teams scale their agentic workflows across enterprise environments.
top_news.image_alt: Screenshot of the AWS Agent Registry dashboard interface

top_news.title: Debian won’t ban AI code from its Linux distribution
top_news.dek: Debian has officially voted to permit the use of AI tools in the development, maintenance, and documentation of its Linux distribution.
top_news.brief: The project's new policy clarifies that generative AI is subject to the same quality and accountability standards as human contributors. Debian maintains that responsible AI usage is acceptable for productivity, provided it adheres to existing project guidelines.

top_news.title: Researchers from Princeton, Ant Group and Stanford Introduce AQuA: A Two-Part Agentic Framework for Autonomous Factor Discovery and Model Development in Quantitative Finance
top_news.dek: Researchers have introduced AQuA, a two-part agentic framework designed to prevent data leakage in autonomous quantitative finance research.
top_news.brief: AQuA addresses the issue where research agents inadvertently corrupt their own training data by propagating 'leaky' features that score well but lack predictive validity. The system uses a dual-agent architecture to decouple experiment generation from evaluation, mitigating shared blind spots.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing the AQuA dual-agent architecture

top_news.title: PRs NOT Welcome: How Top AI Open Source Projects Are Managing Thousands of Contributors
top_news.dek: Leading AI-native open source projects are shifting away from community pull requests in favor of automated, agent-driven development workflows.
top_news.brief: Projects like Vercel’s AI SDK and Astro are increasingly replacing manual community contributions with 'software factories' where AI agents handle fixes and feature implementation. This shift marks a departure from the traditional open-source model of accepting external pull requests.
top_news.image_alt: Abstract representation of automated software development
